prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell's own machinery removes the protein

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation remains the strongest case on the shortlist because one physical-chemical principle, induced proximity, turns occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven, catalytic removal of a protein, and it reaches targets that inhibitors cannot. It is quantitative (ternary-complex cooperativity, geometry and degradation kinetics), it has been confirmed independently by many groups across many ligases and targets for two decades, and it can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence. It is also the only shortlisted achievement that all eight members ranked at opening, and six of eight now include it in their preferred configuration, one above the majority threshold. After the first round I have changed my third name from Handa to Ciulli. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the modality. Ciulli turned it into rational chemistry: the first VHL small-molecule ligands, the first fully small-molecule degraders, and the crystal structures and cooperativity analysis of the ternary complex that explain why a degrader works. That is the quantitative, explanatory layer I look for as a physicist, and it is not implied by the 2001 concept paper.
statement.case_against: Credit is still the weak point. Three names cannot cover Sakamoto and Kim (co-authors of the founding 2001 paper), Handa and Ito (cereblon as the thalidomide target), or Gray. Moving to Ciulli makes the prize PROTAC-centred and leaves the molecular-glue arm, the only one with approved drugs today, without a laureate; a careful reader will notice that and I do not think the citation wording fully repairs it. Clinical maturity is the second weakness: no heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so the case rests on mechanism, breadth of independent confirmation and trial activity. If the committee judges that a PROTAC prize is premature without an approval, the honest consequence is to wait, not to widen the citation until it stops being precise.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that the PROTAC and glue lineages are separable and should not be merged in one citation, and that Handa instead of Ciulli leaves the rational-design chemistry without a name.
responses.response: Johan's argument moved me. I held Handa in round 1 because I wanted one citation covering both mechanisms, but a mechanism discovery about an existing drug and a designed general modality are different claims, and a citation stretched across both risks being imprecise about who discovered what. His point that Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure-guided design are the chemistry core also fits my own test of a quantitative principle. I now accept a PROTAC-centred citation and agree that the glue lineage may deserve separate consideration in a later year.

responses.point: Zou keeps Handa beside Crews and Deshaies, argues that PROTACs and glues meet at the same E3 recruitment mechanism, and asks whether I see a principled way to choose between Handa and Ciulli.
responses.response: Xiaodong asked for a principled criterion, and I owe one. Mine is what each person established that the other two names do not imply: Handa identified the target of an existing drug, which is a major finding, but Ciulli's work supplies the design rules and structural thermodynamics that make induced proximity a general chemical principle usable by others. I still agree with her that the two lineages share a mechanism, and I do not claim glues are unimportant. Where I now differ is that I think the citation is more defensible when it names the designed modality and its structural basis than when it joins two discoveries with different priority histories. I would not object if she keeps Handa on the final ballot, but I would ask her to say what citation wording makes that a single discovery.

responses.point: Aili would honour the PROTAC core with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, accepts that glue degraders are partly left out, and notes that two decades of independent confirmation make recognition timely.
responses.response: I now share Daniel's configuration and his timing argument. His point that PROTACs are a transferable design principle anyone can use against a chosen target is the stronger chemistry argument, and I would accept his suggestion that the citation say small molecules recruit E3 ligases without restricting itself to one compound class, which keeps the door open for glues without crediting them. My remaining concern is the one he states: the glue arm is where approved drugs exist, and the citation should not imply that it has been judged and found lacking.

responses.point: Chabes prefers a two-part prize with B014 for Crews and Deshaies and B042 for Liu alone, and asks whether two chemical-biology parts in one year are acceptable.
responses.response: I agreed in round 1 that Liu alone is the cleaner attribution for base editing, and I still think it is, but I do not support adding it as a second part this year. Two parts from chemical biology and drug discovery in one year would read as one neighbourhood recognised twice, which is his own objection. Base editing also sits next to the 2020 genome-editing prize, and the argument for what is chemically distinct, a deaminase acting on a Cas-bound single-stranded window with no double-strand break, is persuasive but not yet settled for the committee as a whole. Keeping Crews and Deshaies with Ciulli in one part also avoids his two-name PROTAC part, which omits the structural chemistry. I keep B042 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B025 (Gray and Winkler), valuing a physically stated principle over a tool or modality, and concedes that it builds on Marcus theory and Dutton's work.
responses.response: I take Peter's criterion seriously because it is close to my own: I want a stated principle and quantitative evidence. The Gray-Winkler distance and driving-force dependence is exactly that. My difficulty is the one he raises himself, that the question of what is new beyond Marcus theory and natural-protein work has not been answered, and that only one opening ballot ranked it first. I judge that induced proximity also meets the principle test through ternary-complex cooperativity, and it adds a new capability, so I keep B025 outside my configuration.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Buchwald and Hartwig for Pd-catalysed C-N coupling paired with Liu alone for base editing, and omits B014.
responses.response: Peter makes the cleanest attribution case on the list and I agree Kosugi should not be in it. My question stays the one I asked in round 1: what new capability does this add beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and how many drug or process routes depend on it? Aqvist's reply that C-N bond formation needed distinct ligand design and mechanism is a fair answer, so I no longer call B057 merely incremental. Even so, I do not rank it above degradation for generative potential this year, and I would hold it for the committee's expert report rather than add it as a second part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that a PROTAC-centred citation without a glue laureate is defensible, given that approved degrader drugs are glues.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes the PROTAC arm premature; I judge the independent confirmation sufficient but cannot rule out that others will want to wait.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name; I changed to Ciulli on the strength of the structural and design contribution, but the choice is a judgement about credit, not an established fact.
How to acknowledge Sakamoto, Kim, Ito and Gray, who appear in no member's configuration.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I have no stated connection to Crews, Deshaies or Ciulli. I disclose that I am a nanophysicist and that nanopore sequencing (B048) is close to my device interests, though it is not in my configuration. Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr are Lund colleagues, but none of this touches B014.
